frames.narration: The team agrees what to measure: the share of checkout requests that succeed. This is the SLI. It reflects what users experience.
They set the objective: 99.9% of requests succeed over 30 days. This is the SLO.
That leaves an error budget: 0.1% of requests may fail, about 43 minutes of full outage in the 30 days. The budget is full at the start of the window.
A bad deploy causes 20 minutes of failures. Monitoring subtracts them from the budget.
A provider blip and a slow day take most of the rest. Monitoring warns that the budget is burning faster than an even spend would allow.
The budget is spent. By the policy everyone agreed in advance, feature releases pause and the team works on reliability until the service is back within its objective.
Later, with budget left over, the team can ship faster and take risks. The budget makes reliability and speed a trade the team chooses, not an argument.
